elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The exception permits assignments to successors in specified transactions but contains no affiliate-assignment right.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The notwithstanding paragraph permits either party to assign to a successor in a merger upon written notice, overriding the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The notwithstanding paragraph permits either party to assign to a successor in an acquisition upon written notice, overriding the consent requirement.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: The notwithstanding paragraph expressly permits assignment to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets upon written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign this Agreement without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may assign without Customer consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments subject to consent, the clause expressly states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign this Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no prohibition on assignment to a Customer competitor, including where the competitor is a qualifying successor.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no termination right upon Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger upon written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The exception grants either party this right upon written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor in an acquisition upon written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The exception grants either party this right upon written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The exception grants either party this right upon written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor in a merger upon written notice to Customer.
elements.evidence: The exception grants either party this right upon written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor in an acquisition upon written notice to Customer.
elements.evidence: The exception grants either party this right upon written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may assign this Agreement to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets upon written notice to Customer.
elements.evidence: The exception grants either party this right upon written notice.

elements.element: Customer must obtain Vendor's consent for assignments other than the permitted successor assignments, and Vendor may not unreasonably withhold that consent.
elements.evidence: The original mutual prior-written-consent requirement remains operative for other assignments and states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor must obtain Customer's consent for assignments other than the permitted successor assignments, and Customer may not unreasonably withhold that consent.
elements.evidence: The original mutual prior-written-consent requirement remains operative for other assignments and states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the fallback through a mutual successor-assignment exception conditioned on written notice, while retaining consent not to be unreasonably withheld for other assignments. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits Customer's affiliate-assignment right, allows Vendor successor assignments without Customer consent, and lacks an absolute prohibition on Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor. The redline is minimal and preserves the remaining assignment, transfer, and subcontracting restrictions.
